paper.title: Linear Submodular Maximization with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Submodular Maximization with a Cardinality Constraint (SM) with noisy (bandit) queries
unmapped: Objective f = sum_i w_i F_i with known monotone submodular basis functions F_i (value-oracle access) and unknown nonnegative weights w; learner queries noisy marginal gains Delta f(S,x) = Delta F(S,x)^T w + noise for any chosen (S,x)
Goal: output a set S with |S| <= kappa satisfying f(S) >= (1-1/e)f(OPT) - epsilon w.p. >= 1-delta using few samples (PAC-style approximation guarantee)
settings.definition_quote: Let $U$ be a universe of elements of size $n$. Suppose we have $d$ monotone and submodular functions ... $f(S)=\sum_{i=1}^dw_iF_i(S)$ ... We do not have oracle access to $f$, but we may make i.i.d. R-sub-Gaussian noisy queries to $f$ where the expectation is the true value of $f$.

source.label: thm:greedy
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the following statements hold: 1. The exact function value of the output solution set $S$ satisfies that $f(S)\geq(1-e^{-1})f(OPT)-\epsilon.$

results.notes: Approximation guarantee: (1-1/e)OPT - f(S) <= epsilon w.p. >= 1-delta. Recorded as quantity 'other' with expression the additive slack.

symbols.sum_pairs: sum over l' in [l] and a in [n] (past rounds and elements)
symbols.H_la: H_{l',a}^{(l)} = max_{i,j} p*(l',a|l,i,j) rho_{i,j}^l / max{eps/kappa, (Delta_{l,i} v Delta_{l,j} + eps/kappa)/3}^2
symbols.M_l: M^{(l)} = 16 H_eps R^2 L^2/lambda log(1/delta) + 32 H_eps^2 R^4 L^4/lambda^2 + 2(N^{(l)}+n l)L^2/(lambda d) + 2
symbols.N_la: number of samples of Delta F(S_{l'},a) taken before round l

source.label: thm:greedy
source.quote: Assuming $\lambda\leq\frac{2R^2}{S^2}\log\frac{1}{\delta}$, then \alg at round $l$ takes at most $\sum_{l'\in[l],a\in[n]}\max\{4H^{(l)}_{l',a} R^2(2\log\frac{1}{\delta}+d\log M^{(l)})+1-N_{l',a}^{(l)},0\}$ number of samples

results.notes: Per-round sample complexity of LG at round l, w.p. >= 1-delta. R mapped to sigma. Depends on random past sample counts.

symbols.alpha_thr: threshold decrease parameter alpha of LinTG

source.label: thm:threshold
source.quote: \algthre makes $n\log(\kappa/\alpha)/\alpha$ evaluations of the marginal gains. In addition, with probability at least $1-\delta$ ... The function value of the output solution set $S$ satisfies that $f(S)\geq(1-e^{-1}-\alpha)f(OPT)-2\epsilon.$

results.notes: Approximation guarantee relative to (1-1/e-alpha)OPT with additive slack 2 epsilon. The proof in the appendix actually derives -2*kappa*epsilon; recorded as stated in theorem. Also makes n log(kappa/alpha)/alpha marginal-gain evaluations.

symbols.sum_evals: sum over i in [m_eval], the previously evaluated marginal-gain vectors
symbols.m_eval: index of the current marginal-gain evaluation
symbols.H_i: p*_i rho^{(m)} / max{(eps/kappa + |w_thr - Delta F(S,a)^T w|)/2, eps/kappa}^2
symbols.M_m: 16 H_eps R^2 L^2/lambda log(2/delta) + 32 H_eps^2 R^4 L^4/lambda^2 + 2(N^{(m)}+m)L^2/(lambda d) + 2
symbols.N_i: number of samples of the i-th marginal gain before the m-th evaluation

source.label: thm:threshold
source.quote: Assuming $\lambda\leq\frac{2R^2}{S^2}\log\frac{2}{\delta}$, the $m$-th evaluation of the marginal gain of adding an element $a$ to $S$ in \algthre takes at most $\sum_{i\in[m]}\max\{4H^{(m)}_{i} R^2(2\log\frac{2}{\delta}+d\log M^{(m)})+1-N_{i}^{(m)},0\}$ samples

results.notes: Per-evaluation sample complexity of LinTG. R mapped to sigma.

source.label: thm:static
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the following statements hold: 1. The exact function value of the output solution set $S$ satisfies that $f(S)\geq(1-e^{-1})f(OPT)-\epsilon.$

results.notes: Approximation guarantee for static-allocation warm-up algorithm LBSS.

symbols.n: number of elements in the universe U

source.label: thm:static
source.quote: During each round in \algstat, the number of samples required is upper bounded by $$t\leq\max\{\frac{256R^2d}{\max\{\Delta_{\min}^2,\epsilon^2/\kappa^2\}}\log(\frac{256R^2d\pi n}{\max\{\Delta_{\min}^2,\epsilon^2/\kappa^2\}}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{3\delta}}),\frac{d+d^2+2}{2}\} $$ where $\Delta_{\min}=\min_{\{x'\in [n],x'\neq x^*\}}\vect{F}_{x^*}^T\vect{w}-\vect{F}_{x'}^T\vect{w}$

results.notes: Per-round sample count; Delta_min is the per-round gap between the best marginal gain and the others in the current round. R mapped to sigma.
